author: simulation_agent

inequalities.inequality: dt << gamma / u''(a) at the stiffest point of the sweep

note: Three bounds on one parameter, and S4 takes the tightest; all three are recorded because which one binds moves across the sweep. At the stiff corner the curvature bound is five decades below the Brownian one -- the whole reason bd_overdamped's A1 could not be reused here.

numbers.name: bead_diameter
numbers.note: the lab's particles, measured by the operator on 2026-09-19 (CV at most 2 per cent). Taken from the store under the S2 id as the physical-units anchor; see the constraint note on anchoring

numbers.name: diffusivity
numbers.note: the free diffusivity D0 of one particle in the bath; the Brownian time at the mean spacing, a^2/D0, is the natural time unit of the relaxation and every axis derives it from this

numbers.name: spacing_over_diameter
numbers.note: mean centre-to-centre spacing in diameters; sets the area fraction, about 0.2 for a triangular arrangement at 2

numbers.name: mean_spacing
numbers.note: a = rho**-1/2 at the reference density; the density sweep moves it by less than a decade

numbers.name: brownian_time
numbers.note: the time to diffuse one spacing: the natural unit of structural relaxation here, and NOT tau_d, which is the time to diffuse one diameter and belongs to the free-tracer question

numbers.name: gamma_max
numbers.note: the largest U0/kT in the sweep; the stiff corner A1 must survive

numbers.name: kappa_a_max
numbers.note: the shortest range in the sweep, as kappa times the mean spacing

numbers.name: curvature_factor
numbers.note: a**2 u''(a) / kT for u = U0 (a/r) exp(-kappa (r-a)); the ratio of the Brownian time to the curvature relaxation time

numbers.name: curvature_time
numbers.note: gamma / u''(a): the shortest characteristic time in the system at the stiff corner, five decades below tau_B

numbers.name: dt_resolution_factor
numbers.note: how far below the shortest resolved time the step sits

numbers.name: dt_max_brownian
numbers.note: the bound the free-tracer configuration would have stopped at; here it is the loosest of three

numbers.name: noise_step_fraction
numbers.note: the rms noise displacement per step as a fraction of the screening length

numbers.name: dt_max_noise
numbers.note: sqrt(2 D0 dt) must stay inside the potential's range or a step carries a particle across it in one move

assumptions.statement: Two diameters of spacing is a reference density where a 2D Yukawa suspension is neither dilute nor jammed, so the sweep in strength and range has room on both sides. Nothing physical picks it; the density is one of the swept parameters and this is the point about which it is swept.
assumptions.falsifier: a person naming the area fraction of interest, or a first run showing the plateau unreachable at this density inside budget, moves the reference

assumptions.statement: The person left the ranges to S3. Gamma from 10 to 1000 spans the 2D Yukawa fluid, its ordering, and a stiff crystal; kappa a from 1 to 10 spans long-ranged to nearly hard. The stiff corner, Gamma 1000 at kappa a 10, is what the timestep has to survive, and the bound scales as 1/(Gamma (kappa a)**2) away from it.
assumptions.falsifier: a first run showing psi6 already at its plateau at the lowest Gamma, or unreachable inside budget at the highest, moves the corresponding end by a decade

assumptions.statement: Two decades below the shortest resolved time is the usual margin for an overdamped integrator with a stiff repulsion; a convention, not a derivation, and no timestep scan on this model has been run.
assumptions.falsifier: a timestep scan showing the relaxation time flat over a wider range of steps replaces the factor with a measured one

assumptions.statement: A tenth of a screening length per step keeps the force felt during a step close to the force at its start. Looser than the curvature bound at this corner, and recorded because at small Gamma it is the one that binds.
assumptions.falsifier: energy drift or overlap counts flat against step size at larger fractions retires it

kb_refs.claim: The particles in the bottle in use have a diameter of 5 micrometres, with a coefficient of variation no greater than 2 per cent, measured directly by the operator on 2026-09-19.
